summary:
**Healthy Monitoring for Astronauts: AI-Powered Astronaut Health Monitoring System**

Healthy Monitoring for Astronauts is an intelligent health-monitoring platform designed to support astronaut safety during space missions. The project combines a real-time dashboard, simulated wearable sensors, IoT communication, and artificial intelligence to monitor key health indicators, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), ECG, body surface temperature, respiratory rate, skin conductance (GSR), and physical activity.

The system addresses the challenge of continuously monitoring astronauts in demanding space environments, where early detection of unusual physiological changes is essential. It collects simulated health data from multiple astronauts, transmits it through MQTT, and uses AI-based anomaly detection to identify unusual patterns and generate alerts. Mission teams can monitor up to ten astronauts simultaneously through a centralized dashboard.

This project is important because it demonstrates how IoT and AI technologies can improve remote health monitoring, support faster decision-making, and contribute to astronaut safety.
details:
Healthy Monitoring for Astronauts

AI-Powered Astronaut Health Monitoring System

1. Project Function and How It Works

Healthy Monitoring for Astronauts is an intelligent health-monitoring system designed to support astronaut safety during space missions. It uses simulated wearable sensors, IoT communication, artificial intelligence, and a centralized dashboard to monitor astronauts' physiological conditions in real time.

The system monitors several health indicators, including:

  • Heart Rate (BPM).
  • Blood Oxygen Saturation (SpO₂).
  • Electrocardiogram (ECG).
  • Body Surface Temperature.
  • Respiratory Rate.
  • Galvanic Skin Response (GSR).
  • Physical Activity and Movement.

Data is collected from simulated sensor devices connected to ESP32 microcontrollers or generated through software-based astronaut simulations. The readings are transmitted using the MQTT protocol to a backend system, where they are processed, stored, and analyzed by an AI-based anomaly detection model.

The dashboard allows mission control teams to monitor up to ten astronauts simultaneously, view live health indicators, track historical data, and receive alerts when unusual physiological patterns are detected.

2. Project Benefits

  • Continuous monitoring of multiple astronauts through one centralized platform.
  • Early identification of unusual physiological changes.
  • Faster communication of potential health concerns to mission control.
  • Historical health data tracking and analysis.
  • Reduced dependence on manual health monitoring.
  • A scalable architecture that can support additional astronauts and sensors.

3. Expected Impact

The project aims to contribute to astronaut safety by providing mission control teams with better visibility into astronauts' health conditions.

It can help identify potentially concerning changes earlier, support informed decision-making, and improve health-monitoring capabilities during long-duration space missions.

The simulation environment also provides a way to test different health scenarios, communication failures, and emergency situations before deploying similar technologies in real-world environments.

4. Technologies, Programming Languages, and Tools

Programming Languages:

  • Python: Backend development, data processing, simulation, and AI.
  • C/C++: ESP32 firmware and sensor integration.
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: Frontend and dashboard development.

Hardware and Electronics:

  • ESP32 microcontroller.
  • MAX30102 for heart rate and SpO₂ simulation.
  • AD8232 for ECG signal acquisition or simulation.
  • MLX90614 for infrared surface-temperature measurement.
  • MPU6050 for movement and orientation monitoring.
  • GSR sensor for skin conductance.
  • Respiratory sensor for breathing-rate monitoring.

Software and Platforms:

  • Wokwi: ESP32 and electronic circuit simulation.
  • MQTT / Mosquitto: Communication between simulated devices and the backend.
  • Node-RED: Data flow management and integration.
  • FastAPI: Backend and API development.
  • SQLite: Data storage.
  • Scikit-learn: AI-based anomaly detection.
  • Chart.js: Real-time data visualization.

5. Creative and Innovative Aspects

The innovative aspect of Healthy Monitoring for Astronauts is the integration of multiple health indicators into one intelligent monitoring environment.

Instead of treating each sensor as an independent device, the system combines different physiological signals and uses AI-based anomaly detection to identify unusual patterns that may not be obvious when examining individual readings.

Another important feature is its multi-astronaut simulation capability, allowing mission control teams to monitor up to ten virtual astronauts simultaneously. The system can simulate different health scenarios, such as elevated heart rate, reduced oxygen saturation, irregular breathing, unusual movement, and communication interruptions.

This approach makes it possible to test the monitoring system under different mission conditions without requiring a complete set of physical medical devices.

6. Factors Considered by the Team

During the design and development process, the team considered several important factors:

  • Astronaut Safety: Prioritizing early detection of unusual health indicators.
  • Reliability: Handling missing data, communication interruptions, and device disconnections.
  • Real-Time Performance: Ensuring that health data reaches the dashboard with minimal delay.
  • Scalability: Supporting multiple astronauts and allowing future expansion.
  • Data Privacy and Security: Protecting sensitive health information through secure communication and controlled access.
  • Accuracy and Limitations: Recognizing that simulated readings and experimental AI models are not medical diagnoses.
  • Space Environment: Considering the challenges of remote monitoring, limited resources, and long-duration missions.

Conclusion

Healthy Monitoring for Astronauts combines IoT, artificial intelligence, software engineering, and simulation technologies to explore a smarter approach to astronaut health monitoring. Its goal is to support safer space missions by providing continuous health-data visibility, intelligent anomaly detection, and a scalable platform for future development.
